questions.question: You’re waiting in line at a café, and the person in front of you drops their bag. What would be the most appropriate response if you wanted to help without being too intrusive?
options: ‘Excuse me, could you please move your bag a bit? I’ll take that.’
‘Oh dear, that’s a bit messy. I’ll help you sort it out.’
‘That’s not my fault. You should have kept it on the table.’
‘I’m sorry, I didn’t see that coming. Let’s go inside and get coffee.’
questions.answer: ‘Oh dear, that’s a bit messy. I’ll help you sort it out.’

questions.question: Your friend suggests going to a concert next weekend, but you’re not interested. What is the most polite way to politely decline?
options: ‘No, I don’t like concerts. I’d rather stay at home.’
‘I’m sorry, but I can’t go—I’ve got plans with my family.’
‘That sounds boring. I’ll just watch a movie instead.’
‘I don’t want to go. It’s too expensive anyway.’
questions.answer: ‘I’m sorry, but I can’t go—I’ve got plans with my family.’

questions.question: Your colleague asks if you’d like to join them for lunch after work. What would be the most appropriate response if you’re busy but want to be polite?
options: ‘Yes, that would be great! I’ll bring you some salad.’
‘I’m sorry, I can’t make it this time—I’ve got a meeting.’
‘I’d love to, but I’ll have to cancel my plans instead.’
‘No, I don’t like eating with colleagues.’
questions.answer: ‘I’m sorry, I can’t make it this time—I’ve got a meeting.’

questions.question: You’re at a formal dinner and the host asks if everyone would like to try a dessert. What is the most appropriate way to politely decline?
options: ‘I’m afraid I can’t eat any more, thank you.’
‘No, I don’t like desserts—I’ll just have water.’
‘I’m sorry, I’m on a diet, so I won’t have any.’
‘I’ll pass, but I’ll have a coffee instead.’
questions.answer: ‘I’m afraid I can’t eat any more, thank you.’

questions.question: A stranger asks you for directions to the nearest bus stop. What is the most appropriate way to offer help?
options: ‘I’m sorry, I don’t know—I’ll ask someone else.’
‘The bus stop is just down that road. You’ll see it on your left.’
‘You shouldn’t be asking strangers for directions. Just use a map.’
‘That’s not my problem. I don’t know where it is.’
questions.answer: ‘The bus stop is just down that road. You’ll see it on your left.’
